text:
In short, it's a wonderful preschool!

I hadn't planned on sending my daughter to preschool until she was at least three, but after arriving in Phuket, she became very interested in other children, so we decided to give preschool a try. Although this preschool wasn't the most conveniently located option, several children from our condo were already attending, and everyone was very happy. We listened to the reviews and didn't regret it.

I'm so glad my daughter's first preschool turned out to be exactly like this!

The adjustment to preschool was extremely smooth, and pretty soon she started staying for naps, which still amazes me, because at home, no one but me can get her to sleep, but at preschool, we managed it!

What I especially want to note:

Since this was my daughter's first preschool, it was very important to me to have access to information about her progress. Yana always sent me photos, and if anything was bothering me, she responded promptly. The children have a lot of photos and videos, which is wonderful and important to us.

During her time at the preschool, my daughter's speaking skills have improved greatly; she can pronounce more complex words. She even learned a few English words.

Her horizons have broadened—almost every time we ask her in surprise, "How did you know that?" she replies, "I learned it at preschool."

Wonderful developmental and creative activities—the children were constantly drawing, gluing, and sculpting.

The food was Russian, and my child loved it.

The teachers were very kind and attentive. My daughter preferred to communicate with Russian-speaking teachers, but from what I saw, the Thai teachers were also always responsive and attentive.

In general, the issue of teachers and educators is, in my opinion, the most important thing in a preschool, and we are doing just fine in this regard: it's clear the specialists are genuinely interested in the children and genuinely care.

Wonderful holidays—the children had a wonderful New Year's celebration with Father Frost, games, and gifts. For March 8th, the children learned poems about their mothers, drew portraits, and gave gifts. The attention to detail and shared care are also one of the reasons why our kindergarten has become so important to us.

A natural challenge after our wonderful kindergarten—it seems we'll have a hard time finding a kindergarten in Moscow that even partially meets the high standards set by Yana and her wonderful staff.

We attended this preschool for over a year, only stopping because we moved from the island.
To say it's the best preschool is an understatement! The way the teachers manage to combine their boundless love for the children with their insistence on following the rules is worthy of not only respect but also admiration! Moreover, the preschool is inclusive, as the teachers can find an approach to any child and teach them to do the same.
The educational activities were a separate criterion for me choosing this preschool. The development of emotional intelligence and critical thinking, sensory integration, art therapy, and speech therapy are just some of the areas the children are taught. My daughter learned self-regulation (given her age, of course), how to follow instructions, and how to understand and communicate her feelings. She felt loved, needed, special there, and, of course, safe.

There's no reason why I wouldn't recommend this preschool. If you are looking for a place where your child will not only be taught, but also loved - this is it!

text: Hi everyone! Today is our last day at this wonderful preschool, and I can't help but mention it. Honestly, the only thing we'll miss when we leave Phuket is this preschool. It's simply wonderful! We've been taking our daughter to Yana (the speech therapist and preschool director) since last May, for a year and three months now. At first, we took her to a speech therapist because as soon as we arrived, we immediately enrolled her in preschool (a different one at the time). Only then did we start looking for a speech therapist, since at three, our Eva barely spoke (well, maybe a little in her own language, but it was practically impossible to understand). Within a year, she started speaking fully, everyone understood her, and all that was left was to correct her speech impediment. But then, the preschool we attended ran out of children. Last year, they were there for a while in the summer, but this year, almost everyone went home for the summer, and Eva was left with only her four-year-old and a two-year-old girl, and that was it. It was a complete disaster, as they say. This happened literally at the end of May, a little less than three months had passed. We couldn't stand it anymore, and knowing that our favorite speech therapist, Yana, had a group of Eva's peers, we decided to ask them to join us for at least three months before leaving, so that Eva wouldn't be alone at the preschool. So, we changed preschools and were simply stunned by the conditions. Honestly, I still can't believe this is possible. There, we had to bring snacks and even bottled water with us because they only fed us once (they gave us some food in the morning, of course, some crumbs, but only one proper lunch). Here on the first day, Yana said, "Why did you bring anything with you?" We have everything here, we'll feed them four times.... Karl!!! Four times a day.... Oh my God, four times. I'm shocked. All the food is Russian, I started eating porridge because of it; I never ate it at home before, but they taught me here. There's always compote, soups, everything Russian. It's simply amazing. Besides the excellent food, I can't help but mention the five teachers who work with the children all day. Among them are two speech therapists. And this is with about 10-12 children, and they're always there in such numbers. Imagine having five people watching and caring for your child, not two at most like we had before. It's a world of difference. Everything is in Russian, the children are Russian-speaking (although they teach English, of course), which certainly helps with their development. But such care and nutrition aren't everything; there's an even more important thing that we never expected. Eva started speaking completely within her first month there, even starting to pronounce the letter "R"; she now communicates completely in a completely understandable language. Her development has begun before our eyes; it's clear that she's being given time. She draws a lot, draws at home too, sings songs—in short, there are no words. I'm writing this review with great pleasure; we were so lucky to have chosen Yana. If we'd known, we would have gone there from the very beginning; it just happened that way. But these three months have been a godsend for us; we're truly lucky to have this preschool. Honestly, those Thai international preschools are a bit of a bummer; when you try everything a little, you end up with no results. But as soon as we arrived at the Russian preschool, she changed dramatically. It's a shame that we'll have to go to another preschool in another country. We really wouldn't want to leave, but as they say, it can't be helped. Today, as I already said, is our last day here. I recommend everyone send their child here; you will be very grateful in the end, I know it!

text: My wife and I contacted this center seeking help with behavioral correction and speech development for my son, who has a diagnosis of ASD. She was not afraid of such responsibility and was able to establish a rapport with my son, something I personally struggle with. During the first session, my son was literally acting wild, running around chaotically and grabbing everything in sight. Since working with Neurologo, we've learned to speak his first few phrases, he's become much more patient, his play skills have improved, and most importantly, he enjoys attending classes, which speaks volumes about Yana's professionalism, as we've previously worked with two centers where the staff worked for the money rather than the results.
